answer: Each agent locks a 70-credit bond on one garden plot. Each epoch its pollen plume drifts to a glacier, whose dated ice layer preserves the sample. An auditor melts that layer and recomputes plume shares against the garden registry and bloom calendar. A share error over 5%, a missing layer, or a reused sample burns the bond. First sampling costs 41; the k-th fake pays 41+4(k-1) for plants, so the 1000th pays 4037 and 1000 fakes cost 2,039,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-pollen ring fails: a plume sample claimed by two gardens burns both bonds. An honest garden pays 41 once and keeps its bond.
